_design_note: M3.12. The sole change from M3.4 is agent.algorithm, q_learning -> double_dqn (route R02_3 -> R02_4). Training is loot-crate with three rule_based_agent opponents, exactly as M3.4. The reason to spend an opponent arm on this: section 7.15.3 showed the tournament bottleneck is survival (M3.4 survives 17.4 percent of rounds) and section 7.21.5 showed double_dqn is the only change measured so far that cuts deaths substantially (-34 percent, and -71 percent on the 'had a plan throughout and still died' class) -- but that was solo. This asks whether the reduction converts into tournament score.

_predeclared_design_numbers.control: runs/m3_4_t02_vs3rb_20260826/ (classic with opponents 2.227, the project's best)
_predeclared_design_numbers.falsification: Score within 0.246 AND survival within a couple of points of 17.4 percent means the solo death reduction does not transfer, and double_dqn should be reported as a solo-only effect.
_predeclared_design_numbers.prediction_score: above 2.227, but the 0.246 threshold applies and this arm is not reproducible (section 7.15.1).
_predeclared_design_numbers.prediction_share: coins_share above M3.4's 0.220; the threshold is 0.022.
_predeclared_design_numbers.reporting: Report all five training-seed distributions, coins_share, and the death split.
_predeclared_design_numbers.resolution_tournament: docs/01 section 7.20: the pooled 450-round classic-with-opponents score has sd 0.089, so two arms need a gap of 0.246; coins_share needs 0.022. Report coins_share alongside score.
_predeclared_design_numbers.the_metric_that_decides_it: scripts/attribute_deaths.py on the classic-with-opponents jobs. M3.4 is 46.9 percent own bomb / 34.0 percent opponent / 17.4 percent survived. If double_dqn's solo death reduction carries over, survival rises.
